description: Interactive step-based parity checker tool for Grade 7 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Number Play. Displays dot-pairing diagrams for even and odd numbers. Six progressive phases: (1) Introduction to parity concept, (2) Even + Even = Even with paired dots, (3) Odd + Odd = Even showing leftover dots combining, (4) Even + Odd = Odd showing one leftover remaining, (5) Consecutive numbers — always different parity so sum is always odd, (6) Summary of all parity addition rules. Each phase shows two groups of dots being combined with animation — dots slide together and pair up, leftover dots glow red. Blue accent (#3b82f6) for even numbers, orange (#f97316) for odd numbers, white background, dark text, light grey separators. Prediction prompt appears before each reveal. Indian school context — uses chapati distribution and book pages as real-world examples. Clean educational design with Nunito font family. Touch-friendly buttons, mobile-responsive layout. 5-colour palette: blue, orange, white, dark grey text, light grey borders.

teaching_notes: Advance one phase at a time. At Step 1, ask the student to name even and odd numbers. At Steps 2-4, enable prediction mode and pause — let the student think before revealing. At Step 5, connect to the textbook example (consecutive page numbers always sum to odd, Martin and Maria's ages). At Step 6, challenge with Lakpa's coin puzzle: odd ₹1 coins + odd ₹5 coins + even ₹10 coins — can the total be ₹205?
instructions_for_student: Watch as each parity combination is revealed with its dot-pairing diagram. At each step, try to predict whether the sum will be even or odd before the answer appears. Pay attention to what happens to the leftover dots — that is the key to understanding parity!
learning_objectives: Understand parity: the property of a number being even or odd
Determine the parity of the sum of two numbers using the dot-pairing model
Know that even + even = even, odd + odd = even, even + odd = odd
Understand why consecutive numbers always have different parity
Apply parity reasoning to solve puzzles like Martin and Maria's age problem
real_world_connections: Chapati distribution — even numbers split equally, odd numbers leave one over
Book page numbers — consecutive pages always sum to odd
Coin puzzles — Lakpa's piggy bank problem
Birthday age puzzles — Martin and Maria
